# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Windows Event Forwarding

Forwards Windows events to a central Windows Event Collector, so that logs are kept out of reach of an attacker on the device.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | Microsoft Learn — 'Use Windows Event Forwarding to help with intrusion detection' and Policy CSP ADMX_EventForwarding/SubscriptionManager; values verified against the settings catalog definitions |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Event_Forwarding.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Event_Forwarding.json) |

> Replace `WEC-SERVER-FQDN-INVULLEN` with the FQDN of the collector (HTTPS: add port 5986 and `IssuerCA=<thumbprint>`). To forward the **Security** log, NETWORK SERVICE needs read access to that channel — this cannot be set through the settings catalog; add the account to the Event Log Readers group (a Local Administrators-style construction via Account Protection) or set the ChannelAccess SDDL with a script. A WinRM listener does not need to be enabled: Remote Access Hardening turns `allowremoteservermanagement` off, and source-initiated forwarding uses the outbound WinRM client.
